tools.name: Advizeo
tools.positioning: Energy management that ends in a works order — engineering-led rather than reporting-led.
tools.description: Advizeo, part of the Setec engineering group, provides energy monitoring and management for French buildings: meter and building management system data collection, consumption analysis and alerting, décret tertiaire declaration support, and an action plan followed through to implementation.
tools.real_estate_use: Its difference from a pure reporting platform is the engineering behind it. Detecting that a building's heating runs at weekends is only useful if someone changes the schedule. Advizeo pairs the monitoring with technical recommendations and follow-up, which suits owners who do not have an in-house energy engineer.
features: Meter, submeter and building management system data collection
Consumption analysis with drift and anomaly alerting
Décret tertiaire declaration and OPERAT support
Technical action plans with quantified savings
Works and measure follow-up over time
Multi-site portfolio dashboards

use_cases.job: Detect and correct consumption drift instead of only reporting it
Meet décret tertiaire obligations with a costed action plan behind the declaration

tools.name: Deepki
tools.positioning: ESG for real estate portfolios, from data collection to the CRREM trajectory an investor is judged against.
tools.description: Deepki collects and enriches building energy and asset data across a portfolio, benchmarks performance, produces regulatory and investor ESG reporting, and models decarbonisation pathways with the capital expenditure required to reach them.
tools.real_estate_use: European regulation makes this operational rather than reputational: the décret tertiaire requires measured consumption reductions on French tertiary buildings, and the EU taxonomy and SFDR shape what a fund must disclose. Deepki assembles the data across countries and landlord-tenant boundaries — the hardest part, since the landlord often does not hold the tenant's meter data — and turns it into the trajectory and the works plan.
features: Automated collection of energy, water and asset data across a portfolio
Regulatory reporting including décret tertiaire and EU taxonomy alignment
GRESB and investor ESG reporting
CRREM and decarbonisation pathway modelling
Retrofit scenario and capital expenditure planning
Peer benchmarking across a large asset database

use_cases.job: Produce décret tertiaire and EU taxonomy reporting across a European portfolio
Build a costed retrofit plan that puts assets on a compliant carbon trajectory

capabilities: Automated data enrichment and gap filling

tools.name: ENERGY STAR Portfolio Manager
tools.positioning: The free federal benchmarking tool that most US disclosure ordinances are written around.
tools.description: Portfolio Manager is a free online tool from the EPA for tracking energy and water use, waste and emissions in buildings. It produces the 1-to-100 ENERGY STAR score, supports certification applications, and is the submission format required by most US city and state benchmarking laws.
tools.real_estate_use: When a city ordinance requires annual energy disclosure, it almost always means uploading to Portfolio Manager. Owners therefore use it whether or not they have a commercial energy platform — and the commercial platforms exist in part to feed it automatically. The ENERGY STAR score itself is used as a marketing claim in leasing.
features: Free energy, water, waste and emissions tracking
ENERGY STAR 1-to-100 score and certification application
Automated data exchange with utilities and service providers
Compliance reporting for city and state benchmarking laws
Portfolio-level comparison and target setting
Public web services API

use_cases.job: Meet a city benchmarking ordinance at no software cost
Obtain an ENERGY STAR score usable as a leasing and disclosure argument

tools.name: Keyzia
tools.positioning: A French platform for deploying AI use cases across a real estate or construction company, with European hosting and a per-address data layer.
tools.description: Keyzia is a French application that lets a real estate or construction company test, deploy and centralise its AI use cases in one place rather than leaving them scattered across individual accounts. It is sold to estate agents, property administrators and syndics, tradespeople and renovators, banks and insurers, and energy actors, each with its own set of prepared uses: preparing a full listing mandate, analysing quotes and invoices, energy diagnosis, risk and green-value assessment. A module called KeyPark holds a portfolio of addresses with the history attached to each property, covering past transactions, works and diagnostics, with notifications when something changes. An interactive map layer adds address-level data for spotting projects on a territory. The vendor states data is hosted in Europe.
tools.real_estate_use: The AI problem inside a French agency or syndic is not that nobody uses it, it is that everyone uses it separately, in a personal account, with client data. Keyzia is positioned against exactly that: it puts the prepared use cases in one company tool, integrated where the teams already work, so the practice becomes shared rather than hidden. For an agent, the working moment is preparing a mandate: the property's transaction history, its diagnostics, its past works and its surroundings pulled together in minutes instead of an afternoon of portal-hopping. For a property administrator, it is watching a stock of buildings and anticipating which ones will need renovation work. European hosting is a purchase criterion in this market, not a detail.
features: Centralised catalogue of AI use cases deployable across a company
Integration into the business tools the teams already use
KeyPark address portfolio with per-property history of transactions, works and diagnostics
Change notifications on tracked properties
Interactive territory map enriched with address-level data
Quote and invoice document analysis

use_cases.job: Assemble a complete listing mandate from a property's history and surroundings in minutes
Watch a stock of buildings and anticipate which need renovation work
Assess a property's risk and energy value without ordering a study

capabilities: Prepared business use cases for real estate and construction

tools.name: Measurabl
tools.positioning: ESG data for real estate assets, structured for the investor questionnaire that has to be answered every year.
tools.description: Measurabl collects utility and building data, calculates emissions and performance metrics, and produces the disclosures real estate investors are asked for — GRESB, CDP, investor reporting — with physical climate risk scoring and decarbonisation pathway modelling on top.
tools.real_estate_use: A fund's ESG reporting cycle used to mean chasing utility bills across dozens of assets every spring. Measurabl automates the collection, standardises the metrics across countries and unit systems, and generates the submission. The second use is capital planning: modelling which retrofits move an asset off a stranding trajectory before a regulation or a buyer forces the issue.
features: Automated utility data collection and normalisation
Emissions accounting across scopes with portfolio roll-up
GRESB, CDP and investor disclosure reporting
Physical climate risk scoring per asset
Decarbonisation pathway and stranding risk modelling
Capital planning for energy retrofits

use_cases.job: Produce a GRESB submission without chasing utility bills across the portfolio
Identify which assets are on a stranding trajectory and what fixes them

tools.name: SpinalCom
tools.positioning: A building operating system — the layer that makes twenty proprietary building systems queryable as one digital twin.
tools.description: SpinalCom publishes a building operating system that aggregates data from heterogeneous building systems — HVAC, lighting, access, metering, BIM models — into a semantic digital twin, exposed through APIs so applications can be built on top rather than integrated one by one.
tools.real_estate_use: A smart building project usually stalls on the same wall: every subsystem speaks a different protocol and belongs to a different contractor. Placing an operating system between the equipment and the applications means the tenant app, the energy dashboard and the maintenance tool all read the same model of the building, and replacing a supplier does not break everything above it.
features: Aggregation of heterogeneous building systems and protocols
Semantic digital twin linked to the BIM model
Open APIs for third-party applications
Real-time supervision and equipment monitoring
Data historisation for energy and operations analytics
Vendor-independent architecture

use_cases.job: Read every building subsystem through one model instead of twenty interfaces
Build tenant and energy applications on a twin that outlives a supplier change

tools.name: Ubigreen
tools.positioning: Energy and space usage measured together — because an empty floor that is still heated is both problems at once.
tools.description: Ubigreen provides French building operators with energy performance monitoring, regulatory declaration support, and workplace occupancy measurement, combining consumption data with presence and space-use data in one platform.
tools.real_estate_use: Since hybrid work, the two questions arrived together: how much energy does this building use, and how much of it is actually occupied. Measuring both allows the decision that follows — consolidating occupancy onto fewer floors and shutting down the rest, which moves consumption far more than any equipment upgrade.
features: Energy consumption monitoring across multi-site portfolios
Décret tertiaire and OPERAT declaration support
Workplace occupancy and space utilisation measurement
Comfort and indoor environment monitoring
Alerting on consumption drift and equipment faults
Reporting for occupants and management

use_cases.job: Consolidate occupancy onto fewer floors and shut down the energy on the rest
Declare regulated consumption and track the effect of measures taken

tools.name: WatchWire
tools.positioning: Energy and sustainability data management for portfolios where the utility bill itself is the problem.
tools.description: WatchWire aggregates utility invoices, interval meter data and weather data to produce energy analytics, bill validation, budgeting and forecasting, benchmarking submissions and sustainability reporting for commercial portfolios.
tools.real_estate_use: Large portfolios lose money to billing errors and to demand charges nobody notices. WatchWire validates invoices against tariffs and consumption, flags anomalies, and produces the benchmarking submissions that US local ordinances now require — the New York and other city disclosure laws being the practical driver for many buyers.
features: Utility bill capture, validation and exception flagging
Interval meter and weather-normalised analytics
Energy budgeting and forecasting
Local benchmarking ordinance and ENERGY STAR submissions
Emissions accounting and sustainability reporting
Portfolio and asset-level dashboards

use_cases.job: Catch utility billing errors and demand charge anomalies before payment
Meet city benchmarking disclosure obligations across a portfolio

tools.name: Wattsense
tools.positioning: Plug-in connectivity for buildings too small to justify a full BMS integration project.
tools.description: Wattsense provides a hardware and cloud solution that connects a building's existing equipment — boilers, HVAC, meters, controllers — across multiple protocols and exposes the data and control points through a single cloud API, without a bespoke integration project.
tools.real_estate_use: Most of a commercial portfolio is not headquarters buildings. Mid-sized assets have some automation, no standardisation, and no budget for a systems integrator per site. Wattsense targets exactly that middle: a box on site, protocols handled, data and control available remotely — which is what makes portfolio-wide energy management feasible below the flagship tier.
features: Multi-protocol connectivity to existing building equipment
Cloud API for data collection and remote control
Deployment without a bespoke integration project
Remote monitoring and alerting across sites
Data normalisation across heterogeneous equipment
Partner integrations with energy and facility platforms

use_cases.job: Connect mid-sized buildings to remote monitoring without an integration project each
Standardise data collection across a portfolio of heterogeneous equipment
